# Story 43 — Email Communication Channel (Story: CRM-50)

---

## Prerequisites

- Story CRM-99 completed (COM-001 — communication channel model and `TicketMessage.Channel` field).
- Story CRM-27/CRM-28/CRM-29 completed (AUTH-003 — authorization roles used by `TicketMessageEndpoints`).
- Coordinate with the owner of `backend/CRM.Api/CommunicationChannels/` — an `EmailMessage.cs` scaffold already exists there and must be reconciled, not duplicated.
- Coordinate with the owner of `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketMessage*.cs` — the ticket messages endpoint is the surface being extended.

---

## Story Goal

Enable an authorized CRM agent to send an outbound email as a reply on an existing ticket, so that the message appears in the ticket conversation with `Channel = Email` and its delivery status is tracked. Deliverables:

1. A backend `IEmailService` abstraction with a `DevelopmentEmailService` implementation that records outgoing emails instead of calling a real provider, plus configuration hooks for a future SMTP implementation.
2. An `EmailMessageMetadata` record persisted alongside a `TicketMessage` (subject, recipient, `DeliveryStatus`, `ProviderMessageId`, timestamps) — the core `Ticket` entity is **not** modified.
3. Ticket message endpoint extended so that when `channel = Email`, the server derives recipient/subject from trusted server-side data, calls `IEmailService`, records the outcome, and returns an appropriate error on failure (message content preserved on the client).
4. Frontend "Reply Via" selector in `TicketMessagesSection.vue` with an Email compose panel (To / Subject / Message), showing failure UI without discarding the composed text.
5. Ticket history entry ("Email sent to …") when delivery succeeds.

**Out of scope:** incoming email ingestion, email attachments, real SMTP/SendGrid/Graph provider wiring, complex delivery-tracking (bounces, opens), rate-limiting.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** `POST /api/tickets/{id}/messages` records a `TicketMessage` with a `Channel` value (from COM-001). No external delivery is triggered.
- **New behaviour:**
  - When the request specifies `channel = Email`, the backend derives the recipient from the ticket's customer, derives the subject from the ticket title (prefixed `Re: ` if not already), validates that both are usable, then calls `IEmailService.SendAsync`.
  - The `TicketMessage` is persisted with `DeliveryStatus = Pending` **before** the provider call; the same row is updated to `Sent` or `Failed` based on the provider result in the same request (no distributed transaction).
  - On failure the endpoint returns a 502 (or 500) with a user-safe error string; the message row remains with `Failed` status so the agent can retry.
  - Only users holding the agent role (per AUTH-003) may hit this path.

### 6 — Extend the message endpoint

**File:** `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketMessageEndpoints.cs`

In the `POST /api/tickets/{id}/messages` handler:

1. Require the same agent authorization policy already applied (do **not** relax it).
2. Load the ticket and its customer; return 404 if either is missing.
3. If `request.Channel` parses to `Channel.Email`:
   - Resolve `to = customer.Email`. If null/whitespace or fails `MailAddress` parsing → return `400 { code: "customer_email_missing_or_invalid" }`.
   - Reject empty `Content` → `400 { code: "empty_message" }`.
   - Reject `Content.Length > 20000` → `400 { code: "message_too_long" }`.
   - Derive `subject`: `ticket.Subject.StartsWith("Re: ") ? ticket.Subject : $"Re: {ticket.Subject}"`. Ignore any client-supplied recipient.
   - Persist the `TicketMessage` (`Type=AgentMessage`, `Channel=Email`) and an `EmailMessageMetadata` row with `DeliveryStatus = Pending` in one `SaveChangesAsync`.
   - Call `IEmailService.SendAsync`. Catch all exceptions; treat as `Success = false`.
   - Update the metadata row: `Sent` (+ `ProviderMessageId`, `SentAt`) or `Failed` (+ `LastError`), save.
   - On success: append a `TicketHistoryEntry` ("Email sent to {customer.Name}") via the existing history helper; save.
   - On failure: return `502 { code: "email_delivery_failed", messageId }`. The message row stays in `Failed` state so the client can surface an inline error but retain the draft.
4. When `Channel != Email` fall through to the pre-existing logic.

The endpoint must **never** log or echo `EmailOptions.Smtp.Password` or the raw provider error stack. Wrap provider exceptions with `logger.LogError(ex, "Email provider failed for ticket {TicketId}", ticket.Id)` and return only the safe error code.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Customer has no email** — backend rejects with `400 customer_email_missing_or_invalid`; frontend disables Send and shows `noCustomerEmail`. Enforced in `TicketMessageEndpoints.cs` (Task 6) and `TicketMessagesSection.vue` (Frontend Task 2).
- **Invalid email address on customer** — same `400` branch, using `System.Net.Mail.MailAddress` parsing.
- **Empty message body** — `400 empty_message`. Frontend also disables Send when `content.trim().length === 0`.
- **Very long message (>20000 chars)** — `400 message_too_long`. Frontend shows the localized error but keeps the draft.
- **Provider unavailable / timeout / throws** — caught in Task 6; metadata row set to `Failed`, endpoint returns `502 email_delivery_failed`, draft preserved on the client.
- **Provider returns success but with no `ProviderMessageId`** — treat as success with `ProviderMessageId = null`; do not fail the request.
- **Unauthorized user (missing agent role)** — 401/403 enforced by the same policy already on `POST /api/tickets/{id}/messages`; verified by `TicketMessageEndpointsTests` (see Test Plan).
- **Ticket not found / customer not found** — `404`; UI redirects back to list.
- **Expired auth** — existing `http.ts` interceptor already handles 401; no extra work.
- **Half-applied state** (message saved, provider call crashed the process before metadata update) — metadata stays `Pending`; UI surfaces `Pending` and agent can retry by sending a new message. Documented; no auto-retry.
- **Concurrent sends on the same ticket** — no cross-request lock; each request creates its own message row so there is no shared state to corrupt.
- **Secret leakage** — `EmailOptions.Smtp` must never appear in any response body; verify by test that hitting `/api/tickets/{id}/messages` on a `Failed` case returns only `{ code, messageId }`.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration `AddEmailMessageMetadata` adds only the new `email_messages` table. It is additive; rollback = `dotnet ef migrations remove` before deploy, or drop-table on the deployed DB.
- No data backfill required — existing `TicketMessage` rows do not need metadata.
- On a half-applied deploy (new migration, old code): the old code never writes `email_messages`; behaviour unchanged.
- On a half-applied deploy (new code, old DB missing table): the endpoint will 500 for Email channel; keep `Provider = Development` in staging so the failure is contained, and gate the frontend Email option behind a feature flag if a phased rollout is needed (documented as a follow-up; not implemented here).
